blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The paper cites and its reference list names this entry; copied as printed despite potential bibliographic inconsistency.
blind_target.title: The cocktail party phenomenon revisited: Attention and memory in the classic selective listening procedure of Cherry (1953).

blind_target.authors: Conway AR, Cowan N, & Bunting MF
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Replicating the finding of
Conway et al. (2001)
that individual differences in working memory span are related to errors in shadowing after the presentation of one’s own name, low span participants were more likely than high span participants to commit shadowing errors on a relevant to-be-shadowed word location. While this was true regardless of whether participants were classified based on their operation span scores or based on their running span scores, the effect was largest when participants were classified based on both scores combined. Thus it seems the effect is most reliably detected when more than one measure of working memory span is used.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
The retrospective questionnaire proved insensitive to individual differences in working memory, probably because our lowest quartile (
M
operation span = 28.00, range 10-39) was well above the lowest quartile of Conway et al. (
M
operation span = 8.22, range 6-12). Taken together, our findings suggest that errors in shadowing caused by attention recruitment may occur in some individuals without rising to the point of conscious memory of the event.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Shadowing-error individual differences replicated, but retrospective conscious name detection was insensitive to span; the authors explicitly discuss both comparisons.
blind_target.title: The cocktail party phenomenon revisited: The importance of working memory capacity.

blind_target.evidence_quote:
In order to dig deeper into the results obtained by the CPS, I have tried to replicate this part of the
   research. Of course, without access to the CPS dataset there will be some differences from their
   results, but the methodology I have applied is designed to be transparent and robust in its own
   right.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
These numbers are all indicative, prior to any reliability testing, and, of course, they do not
   realistically provide evidence of the existence or absence of bias in the BBC any more than the
   CPS figures do. What they do represent is a fairly simple way to debunk the main conclusions
   drawn by the CPS from their own analysis and then spread by an overly­credulous press.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The contextualisation effects were recovered, but the main argument is that those measures do not establish ideological bias; the report’s overall interpretation is undermined.
blind_target.title: Bias at the Beeb: A quantitative study of slant in BBC online reporting
